placements.name: Quin
placements.lead: During her time on the show, Quin proved to be the season's dominant competitor, winning five maxi challenges while also earning four high placements and two lows. She started strongly alongside Minnie Skurr in the opening "So Emotional" lip sync and later built momentum through wins in rounds that also featured Paige Turner, Ginger Hollywood, Anita Crown Davenport, Velvet Vixen, Cupcakke, and Gigi Cherie. Even after late lows during Ginger Hollywood's Rusical win and Autumnatic's Roast win, she recovered to win the final competitive maxi challenge before the finale. Quin reached the finale with Paige Turner and Autumnatic, and she was crowned the winner.
placements.personality: Quin was barely represented through speech, with no recorded confessionals or house dialogue, so her personality came through almost entirely in how often the edit placed her in performance and judging situations. She read less as a narrator of the season than as a quiet competitive presence, repeatedly appearing beside other major figures without explaining her own strategy or emotions on camera.
trivia: Quin lip synced with Minnie Skurr to "So Emotional" in the opening episode.
She won mini challenges in the Acting Challenge episode and the Stand-Up Challenge episode.
No confessionals or house dialogue were recorded for her thread.

placements.name: Paige Turner
placements.lead: During her time on the show, Paige Turner became one of the season's most consistent finalists, recording one maxi challenge win, six high placements, and one bottom placement. Her win came in the Acting Challenge episode, after which she remained a regular presence near the top alongside Quin, Gigi Cherie, Ginger Hollywood, and Autumnatic. Late in the season, she lip synced with Quin to "Holding Out for a Hero" and with Ginger Hollywood to "Love Shack" while continuing to survive toward the finale. Paige reached the finale with Quin and Autumnatic, placing second as the runner-up when Quin was crowned.
placements.personality: Paige Turner had almost no spoken characterization in the available material, despite being present deep into the season. The edit showed her as steady and frequently involved in major judging moments, but without confessionals or house dialogue, her relationships and reactions were left largely undefined.
trivia: Paige Turner won mini challenges in the Girl Group Challenge, The Roast, and Runway Challenge episodes.
She lip synced with Quin to "Holding Out for a Hero" late in the season.
No confessionals or house dialogue were recorded for her thread.

placements.name: Autumnatic
placements.lead: During her time on the show, Autumnatic placed third, was named Miss Congeniality, and won three maxi challenges while landing in the bottom three times. Her season was also marked by her showmance with Gigi Cherie, a relationship that became especially important as both queens advanced into the late game. Autumnatic survived lip syncs involving Sharon Needles, Anita Crown Davenport, and Gigi Cherie, while also winning key rounds including the Girl Group Challenge, The Roast, and the Stand-Up Challenge. She reached the finale with Quin and Paige Turner, where Quin was crowned the winner.
placements.personality: Autumnatic's only clear interpersonal marker was her showmance with Gigi Cherie, and the record also identified her as Miss Congeniality, but the transcript gave her no dialogue to show how she earned that reputation. On camera, she functioned more as a warm relational presence by association than as a confessional narrator, with her bond with Gigi doing most of the characterization the edit allowed.
trivia: Autumnatic and Gigi Cherie were a showmance during the season.
She lip synced against Gigi Cherie to "Only Girl (In the World)" in the Music Video Challenge episode.
No confessionals or house dialogue were recorded for her thread.

placements.name: Gigi Cherie
placements.lead: During her time on the show, Gigi Cherie placed fourth, earned three high placements, and landed in the bottom once. Her late-season run was closely tied to Autumnatic, her showmance, and she was repeatedly recognized alongside Paige Turner and Quin during the stretch after Velvet Vixen and Anita Crown Davenport left. Gigi's final round placed her in a lip sync against Autumnatic to "Only Girl (In the World)." She was sashayed away before the finale, leaving Quin, Paige Turner, and Autumnatic as the final three.
placements.personality: Gigi Cherie was a quiet late-season presence in the available transcript, with no recorded confessionals or house dialogue of her own. Her personality was therefore defined almost entirely by proximity to Autumnatic; the showmance was the only sustained personal detail attached to her on camera.
trivia: Gigi Cherie and Autumnatic were a showmance during the season.
Her elimination lip sync was against Autumnatic to "Only Girl (In the World)."
No confessionals or house dialogue were recorded for her thread.

placements.name: Ginger Hollywood
placements.lead: During her time on the show, Ginger Hollywood placed fifth, won three maxi challenges, received one low placement, and landed in the bottom three times. She opened her competitive record with a win in the second episode and later added wins in The Rusical and the Runway Challenge. Her trajectory became more unstable late in the game as she moved between wins, lows, and lip sync danger while competing against queens including Quin, Paige Turner, Autumnatic, Anita Crown Davenport, and Gigi Cherie. Ginger's run ended when she lip synced with Paige Turner to "Love Shack" and was sashayed away.
placements.personality: Ginger Hollywood had no recorded dialogue, so her personality was not built through confessionals, jokes, or workroom conflict. What did come through was a volatile competitive edit: she was shown in both triumphant and vulnerable judging positions, making her feel more like a high-variance performer than an interpersonal character.
trivia: Ginger Hollywood's first recorded maxi challenge win came in the same episode where Marge Stache was sashayed away.
She lip synced against Velvet Vixen to "Defying Gravity" and against Paige Turner to "Love Shack."
No confessionals or house dialogue were recorded for her thread.

placements.name: Anita Crown Davenport
placements.lead: During her time on the show, Anita Crown Davenport placed sixth, earned two high placements, received one low placement, and landed in the bottom five times. Her season was marked by a showmance with Velvet Vixen and by repeated lip sync survival, beginning with her early battle against Marge Stache to "Holding Out for a Hero." She later outlasted Cheryl Hole and Cupcakke in lip syncs, while also reaching high points in episodes won by Quin and Sharon Needles. Anita was ultimately sashayed away after lip syncing with Autumnatic to "Freedom! '90."
placements.personality: Anita Crown Davenport was mostly characterized through endurance rather than speech, as the transcript recorded no confessionals or house dialogue from her. Her showmance with Velvet Vixen gave her a specific connection in the cast, while her repeated appearances in lip sync situations made her come across as someone the edit returned to when the season needed survival stakes.
trivia: Anita Crown Davenport and Velvet Vixen were a showmance during the season.
She lip synced to "Holding Out for a Hero," "Believe," "Hung Up," and "Freedom! '90."
No confessionals or house dialogue were recorded for her thread.

placements.name: Velvet Vixen
placements.lead: During her time on the show, Velvet Vixen placed seventh, earned one high placement, received three lows, and landed in the bottom twice. Her run was tied personally to Anita Crown Davenport through their showmance, while competitively she spent several episodes under critique before briefly rising during Ginger Hollywood's Rusical win. As the field narrowed, she fell into danger during Autumnatic's Roast win. Velvet lip synced with Ginger Hollywood to "Defying Gravity" and was sashayed away.
placements.personality: Velvet Vixen was given no recorded confessionals or house dialogue, so her personality remained largely opaque. The only personal context attached to her was her showmance with Anita Crown Davenport, and otherwise she appeared mainly through critique placements and her final lip sync rather than through conversations with the cast.
trivia: Velvet Vixen and Anita Crown Davenport were a showmance during the season.
Her final lip sync was against Ginger Hollywood to "Defying Gravity."
No confessionals or house dialogue were recorded for her thread.

placements.name: Cupcakke
placements.lead: During her time on the show, Cupcakke placed eighth, earned three high placements, and landed in the bottom twice. She began with a strong early stretch, appearing high in episodes won by Ginger Hollywood, Paige Turner, and Autumnatic. Her later record turned more precarious as she lip synced against Minnie Skurr to "Roar" and then Anita Crown Davenport to "Hung Up." Cupcakke was sashayed away after the Snatch Game episode.
placements.personality: Cupcakke did not receive recorded confessionals or house dialogue, leaving little evidence of how she interacted with the other queens. Her edit was mostly that of a visible early performer whose personal perspective disappeared behind the competition structure as the season moved toward her elimination.
trivia: Cupcakke won the mini challenge in the Snatch Game episode.
She lip synced to "Roar" with Minnie Skurr and to "Hung Up" with Anita Crown Davenport.
No confessionals or house dialogue were recorded for her thread.

placements.name: Sharon Needles
placements.lead: During her time on the show, Sharon Needles placed ninth, won one maxi challenge, received one low placement, and landed in the bottom once. She first appeared in danger during Autumnatic's Girl Group Challenge win, then rebounded by winning the Improv Challenge. Her final competitive episode was The Rusical, where Ginger Hollywood won and Sharon fell into the bottom. Sharon lip synced with Autumnatic to "The Beginning" and was sashayed away.
placements.personality: Sharon Needles had no recorded speech in the transcript, so her personality cannot be reconstructed from confessionals or workroom exchanges. Her presence was defined by quick swings in judging attention, with the edit presenting her as a queen who could have a notable challenge moment but little documented interpersonal storyline.
trivia: Sharon Needles won mini challenges in the Commercial Challenge episode and The Rusical episode.
Her elimination lip sync was against Autumnatic to "The Beginning."
No confessionals or house dialogue were recorded for her thread.

placements.name: Minnie Skurr
placements.lead: During her time on the show, Minnie Skurr placed tenth, won one maxi challenge, and landed in the bottom four times. She began the season with immediate impact by winning the opening maxi challenge and lip syncing with Quin to "So Emotional." After that early peak, her thread became dominated by repeated lip syncs against Taystee, Riot, and Cupcakke. Minnie was ultimately sashayed away after lip syncing with Cupcakke to "Roar."
placements.personality: Minnie Skurr's available characterization was almost entirely physical and competitive, not verbal, because she had no recorded confessionals or house dialogue. She stood out as an early focal point and then as a recurring lip sync presence, making her seem central to the season's elimination mechanics even without a spoken point of view.
trivia: Minnie Skurr lip synced with Quin to "So Emotional" in the opening episode.
She later lip synced to "9 to 5," "Point of No Return," "Gypsy Woman," and "Roar."
No confessionals or house dialogue were recorded for her thread.

placements.name: Riot
placements.lead: During her time on the show, Riot placed eleventh, earned one high placement, received one low placement, and landed in the bottom once. Her short run moved from a low in Ginger Hollywood's early win to a high placement in Quin's Commercial Challenge win. The following episode, she fell into the bottom during Autumnatic's Girl Group Challenge win. Riot lip synced with Minnie Skurr to "Point of No Return" and was sashayed away.
placements.personality: Riot's transcript presence was brief and silent, with no recorded confessionals or house dialogue. Because her edit moved quickly through contrasting judging moments, she came across less as a developed house personality and more as a short-run contestant whose time was defined by abrupt shifts in visibility.
trivia: Riot's elimination lip sync was against Minnie Skurr to "Point of No Return."
Her final episode was the Girl Group Challenge with the runway category Structure and Silhouette.
No confessionals or house dialogue were recorded for her thread.

placements.name: Cheryl Hole
placements.lead: During her time on the show, Cheryl Hole placed twelfth, received one low placement, and landed in the bottom once. Her recorded competition thread began with a low placement in the Acting Challenge episode won by Paige Turner. The next episode, Quin won the maxi challenge while Cheryl fell into the bottom. Cheryl lip synced against Anita Crown Davenport to "Believe" and was sashayed away.
placements.personality: Cheryl Hole had one of the thinnest edits in the transcript, with no recorded confessionals or house dialogue and only a short competitive thread. There is not enough evidence to describe her social style, humor, or relationships beyond the fact that she was present for early judging and elimination scenes.
trivia: Cheryl Hole's elimination lip sync was against Anita Crown Davenport to "Believe."
Her two recorded competitive episodes were the Acting Challenge and Commercial Challenge episodes.
No confessionals or house dialogue were recorded for her thread.

placements.name: Taystee
placements.lead: During her time on the show, Taystee placed thirteenth, earned one high placement, and landed in the bottom twice. Her thread included an early lip sync against Minnie Skurr to "9 to 5" and a later high placement during Autumnatic's Girl Group Challenge win. She returned to danger in Quin's later maxi challenge win, again lip syncing with Minnie Skurr. Taystee was sashayed away after the "Gypsy Woman" lip sync.
placements.personality: Taystee's available material gave no direct sense of her voice, because she had no recorded confessionals or house dialogue. Her thread is unusually fragmented, with the record showing both a brief rebound and repeated lip sync danger, so her personality cannot be separated from the mechanics of those appearances.
trivia: Taystee lip synced against Minnie Skurr to both "9 to 5" and "Gypsy Woman."
Her high placement came in the Girl Group Challenge episode.
No confessionals or house dialogue were recorded for her thread.

placements.name: Marge Stache
placements.lead: During her time on the show, Marge Stache placed fourteenth and landed in the bottom once. Her only recorded competitive episode was the one won by Ginger Hollywood, with Quin and Cupcakke also recognized as high. Marge lip synced against Anita Crown Davenport to "Holding Out for a Hero." She was sashayed away at the end of that episode.
placements.personality: Marge Stache had the least developed transcript presence, with no recorded confessionals, house dialogue, or extended interpersonal scenes. The material supports only that she appeared for one early elimination storyline, not enough to infer a social role in the cast.
trivia: Marge Stache's only recorded lip sync was against Anita Crown Davenport to "Holding Out for a Hero."
Her only recorded episode was won by Ginger Hollywood.
No confessionals or house dialogue were recorded for her thread.
